I can’t give a precise percentage without source data — I won’t fabricate numbers. If you can provide the renewal count and the eligible-user count for last quarter (or grant access to the data), I’ll compute it exactly.

How to compute it yourself
- Formula: renewal % = (number of renewals during the quarter ÷ number of users eligible to renew during that quarter) × 100

Example (illustrative only)
- If 1,234 renewals and 5,678 eligible users: (1,234 ÷ 5,678) × 100 = 21.74%

Helpful queries / formulas you can run
- SQL (replace :start_date and :end_date with the quarter dates and adjust column/table names):
  SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN renewed = TRUE AND renewal_date BETWEEN :start_date AND :end_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS renewals,
    SUM(CASE WHEN eligible = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS eligible,
    CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN eligible = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
         ELSE ROUND(
           100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN renewed = TRUE AND renewal_date BETWEEN :start_date AND :end_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
           / SUM(CASE WHEN eligible = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2)
    END AS renewal_pct
  FROM users;

- Excel/Sheets (renewals in A2, eligible in B2):
  =IF(B2=0,"N/A", ROUND(A2/B2*100,2)) & "%"

If you want, paste the renewal and eligible counts (or grant read-only access details), and I’ll compute the exact percentage and format it to the precision you prefer.
